s1.syndrome_frame: Acute psychiatric presentation with fluctuating catatonia-like and psychotic symptoms
salient_findings: Catatonia-like signs with fluctuating mutism and psychomotor retardation
Psychotic signs with auditory hallucinations and thought blocking
Seizure-like behavior with head jerking and eye fluttering
key_facts: 45-year-old woman with history of benzodiazepine use disorder, opiate use disorder, borderline personality disorder, and major depressive disorder
Recently discharged from another facility and had 18 emergency department visits in the prior year
Home medications included clonazepam, clonidine, buprenorphine–naloxone, fluoxetine, gabapentin, and trazodone
Exhibited selective acceptance of certain medications and refusal of others
Showed purposeful movements to obtain lorazepam after seizure-like episodes
Had evidence of self-induced urinary incontinence during one episode
Regional catatonia specialist evaluated her and noted that she was unlikely to have catatonia
Repeated lorazepam challenge tests had limited effect on her behaviors and appeared to reinforce them
